name: Bahamas, The
headline: Bahamas, The: +3.8% growth in 2025, 1.1% inflation, debt 72% of GDP
sections: Bahamas, The is a $17.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 141st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.8% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $41K at purchasing-power parity (2024), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 0.6% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 1.1% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 9.4% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 19.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 72% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −0.5% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −8.3% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 79% of GDP (2024), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.5% of GDP (2024).
IMF projections put government debt at 56% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 74.7 years (2024). Population: 413 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
